together, with sincere hearts, they prostrate themselves, casting their bodies to the ground.
I take refuge in the Great Compassionate Father of the World. Namo Maitreya Buddha; Namo Śākyamuni Buddha;

Namo Ratnaśrī Buddha; Namo Arhat Buddha; Namo Viśokadatta Buddha; Namo Sukhāvatī Buddha; Namo Lokagati Buddha; Namo Priyadarśana Buddha; Namo Supratisthita Buddha; Namo Utpala Buddha; Namo Kusumadāmaka Buddha; Namo Anantaprabhāpratibhāna Buddha; Namo Śraddhārya Buddha; Namo Guṇavīrya Buddha; Namo Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva; Namo Vajragarbha Bodhisattva; Namo Anantakāya Bodhisattva; Namo Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. Furthermore, I take refuge in all the Triple Gem throughout the ten directions, as far as the limits of space.
I pray that you will, through the power of your compassion, likewise grant us your protection and guidance.
May those such as I and others fulfill their aspirations and realize the vows for Bodhi.

Next, I make a vow regarding the faculty of the tongue; next, I make a vow regarding the faculty of the tongue. Furthermore, I pray that today, within this ritual arena, all members of the assembly who share in this same practice may attain [their goals].
Extending widely to all sentient beings throughout the ten directions— those born from the four modes of birth and those within the six realms—
from this moment until they reach Bodhi.
The tongue never tastes the flavor of the bodies of any sentient beings that have been injured or killed;
it never tastes the flavor of anything that has died of its own accord;
it never tastes the flavor of the blood or marrow of living beings.
May I never taste the flavor of poison served by an enemy to my master;
may I never taste the flavors of all those things that give rise to the afflictions of craving and attachment;
and may my tongue always taste the hundred kinds of delicious flavors of nectar.
He constantly tastes the flavors of all naturally occurring foods;
he constantly tastes the flavor of the fragrant rice of the Accumulated Fragrance;
he constantly tastes the flavor of the food consumed by all Buddhas.
They constantly taste the flavors manifested through the cultivation of the Dharma-body’s precepts, concentration, and wisdom;
they constantly taste the flavor of the joy of the Dharma and the bliss of dhyāna;
and they constantly taste the sweet and harmonious flavor that nourishes the life of wisdom through the refinement of immeasurable merit.
They constantly taste the single flavor of liberation and the equal flavor [of all things].
They constantly taste the flavor of the most supreme and victorious flavor of the ultimate bliss of the nirvana of all Buddhas.
Having thus fulfilled their vow regarding the faculty of the tongue.
Together, with sincere hearts, they prostrated themselves fully upon the ground and took refuge in the Great Compassionate Father of the World.

Homage to Maitreya Buddha. Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha. Homage to Satyaka Buddha. Homage to Indradeva Buddha. Homage to Uccaghoṣa Buddha. Homage to Śraddhāviśuddha Buddha. Homage to Vāgīśvara Buddha. Homage to Puṇyamati Buddha. Homage to Arciṣmat Buddha. Homage to Anantaguṇa Buddha. Homage to Rāśivipula Buddha. Homage to Siṃhavikrāmin Buddha. Homage to Akṣobhya Buddha. Homage to Śraddhāviśuddha Buddha. Homage to Ākāśagarbha Bodhisattva. Homage to Sadāprarudita Bodhisattva. Homage to Anantakāya Bodhisattva. Homage to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. Furthermore, I take refuge in the Triple Gem throughout the ten directions, as far as the limits of space.
I pray that by the power of your compassion, you will take pity on us and provide protection, so that [Name] and others may fulfill their aspirations and attain the vow of Bodhi.

Next, I make this aspiration for the faculty of body; next, I make this aspiration for the faculty of body. Furthermore, I pray that today all members of the assembly who share the same practice at this site of enlightenment [may likewise attain fulfillment].
Extending widely to all sentient beings throughout the ten directions,
from this day forth until the attainment of Bodhi,
may my body never again experience the touch of the five desires or their deceptive allurements.
They do not perceive the touch of the boiling cauldrons, the burning coals, or the freezing ice;
they do not perceive the touch of the molten copper poured into their mouths, which burns and sears the heads of hungry ghosts;
and they do not perceive the touch of being flayed and torn apart as animals.
They do not perceive the touch of the four hundred and four diseases or various sufferings;
they do not perceive the touch of unbearable great heat or great cold;
they do not perceive the touch of mosquitoes, gadflies, fleas, lice, and other insects.
May they not perceive the touch of being harmed by swords, staves, or poisons;
may they not perceive the touch of hunger, thirst, or any such suffering.
May their bodies always perceive the touch of the wondrous garments of the devas.
One constantly experiences the natural touch of ambrosia;
one constantly experiences the refreshing touch that is neither cold nor hot;
one constantly experiences the touch of vigor, free from hunger and thirst, and devoid of illness and affliction.
One constantly experiences the touch of peaceful sleep and peaceful awakening, free from sorrow and fear;
one constantly experiences the touch of gentle breezes blowing upon the body in the pure lands of the Buddhas of the ten directions;
and one constantly experiences the touch of bathing the body and mind in pools of the seven treasures within the pure realms of the Buddhas of the ten directions.
One constantly perceives the touch of being free from the sufferings of old age, sickness, and death;
one constantly perceives the touch of flying with mastery while listening to the Dharma together with the bodhisattvas;
and one constantly perceives the touch of the eight masteries of the nirvāṇa of all buddhas.
Having completed the vow of the body-faculty,
we together, with utmost sincerity, prostrate ourselves with our five limbs touching the ground and take refuge in the Great Compassionate Father of the World.

Homage to Maitreya Buddha. Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha. Homage to Cāritramati Buddha. Homage to Nāgaruta Buddha. Homage to Cakradhara Buddha. Homage to Dhanasambhava Buddha. Homage to Lokapriya Buddha. Homage to Dharmakīrti Buddha. Homage to Amitaratnakīrti Buddha. Homage to Meghasvarūpa Buddha. Homage to Prajñāmārga Buddha. Homage to Sugandha Buddha. Homage to Gaganasvara Buddha. Homage to Gaganabuddhi Buddha. Homage to Trailokyavikrāmin Bodhisattva. Homage to Bhadrapāla Bodhisattva. Homage to Anantagātra Bodhisattva. Homage to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. Furthermore, I take refuge in all the Triple Gem throughout the ten directions, as far as the limits of space.
I pray that by the power of your compassion, you will protect and sustain us,
so that [Name] and others may fulfill their aspirations and attain the vow for Bodhi.
Next, I make this aspiration for the assembly of fellow practitioners at today’s site of enlightenment.
Extending broadly to all sentient beings throughout the ten directions,
from this day forth until the attainment of bodhi,
may their minds always recognize that desire, hatred, and delusion are afflictions.
One should always know that killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, false speech, frivolous speech, divisive speech, and harsh speech are afflictions.

One should always know that killing one’s father, harming one’s mother, killing an Arhat, shedding the blood of a Buddha, and causing a schism in the Saṃgha constitute the crimes of immediate retribution (ānantarya).
One should always know that those who slander the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha, and do not believe in the law of cause and effect, death and rebirth, and karmic retribution;
and one should always know how to distance oneself from evil associates and draw near to virtuous friends.
He constantly knows that the teachings of the ninety-six kinds of heterodox teachers are false;
he constantly knows that the dharmas of the three outflows, the five hindrances, and the ten entanglements are obstructions;
and he constantly knows that the three miserable realms are fearsome and that the cycle of birth and death is a place of extreme and bitter retribution.
May they always know that all sentient beings possess Buddha-nature;
may they always know that the Buddhas are great compassionate fathers and unsurpassed kings of physicians;
and may they know that all honored teachings are the excellent medicine for the illnesses of all sentient beings.
All worthy and holy ones act as mothers who care for the sick among sentient beings.
They desire that you always know how to take refuge in the Triple Gem, receive the five precepts, and subsequently practice the ten wholesome deeds.
Such dharmas as these can bring about superior retributions among devas and humans;

yet one must always know that they do not exempt one from birth and death, and should therefore cultivate the seven expedient means, the contemplations on the stages of the *mūrdhan* (summit), and so forth.
One should always know the sixteen noble minds of untainted patience regarding what should be practiced.
First, one cultivates the contemplation of the sixteen aspects to observe the Four Noble Truths;
because one always knows that the Four Truths are equal and signless, one realizes the four fruits of the path.
They constantly know all phenomena in their universal and specific characteristics in every aspect;
they constantly know the twelve links of dependent origination and the revolving cycle of cause and effect across the three periods of time without cessation;
and they constantly know the practice of the six perfections and the eighty thousand modes of conduct.
He constantly knows how to sever the eighty-four thousand afflictions;
he constantly knows how to realize non-arising and thereby necessarily sever birth and death;
and he constantly knows the complete sequence of the stages of the ten abidings.
One should always know that by means of the adamantine mind, one cuts off the darkness of ignorance and attains the unsurpassed fruit.
One should always know that its essence is ultimate singularity; when the myriad virtues are perfectly complete and all afflictions are entirely exhausted, one achieves Great Nirvana.
They constantly know the Buddha-ground’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, eighteen unique qualities, immeasurable merits, and immeasurable wholesome dharmas;
having thus brought their resolve and faculties to fulfillment.
Together, with sincere hearts, they prostrated themselves on the ground,
taking refuge in the Great Compassionate Father of the World.

Homage to Maitreya Buddha. Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha. Homage to Deva-rāja Buddha. Homage to Vimalaprabha Buddha. Homage to Sudhana Buddha. Homage to Dīptārcis Buddha. Homage to Ratnaruta Buddha. Homage to Manujendra-rāja Buddha. Homage to Rāhu-gupta Buddha. Homage to Kṣema Buddha. Homage to Siṃhamati Buddha. Homage to Ratna-yaśas Buddha. Homage to Labdhalābha Buddha. Homage to Samantadarśin Buddha. Homage to Aśvaghoṣa Bodhisattva. Homage to Nāgārjuna Bodhisattva. Homage to Anantagātra Bodhisattva. Homage to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. Furthermore, I take refuge in all the Three Jewels throughout the ten directions, as far as the limits of space.
I pray that you, with a heart of compassion, will look upon us with pity, protect us, and sustain us, so that [name] and others may fulfill their aspirations and attain the vows of Bodhi.
Next, I make this oral vow; next, I make this oral vow; furthermore, I pray for the great assembly.
Extending widely to all sentient beings throughout the ten directions,
from this day forth until the attainment of bodhi,
may my mouth never disparage the Triple Gem.
One does not slander those who widely propagate the sutras by speaking of their faults;
one does not say that performing good deeds does not yield the retribution of happiness, nor that committing evil deeds does not yield the fruit of suffering;
and one does not say that upon death a person is annihilated and will not be reborn again.
One does not speak of matters that are unbeneficial or that harm others.
One does not speak of the scriptures composed by those of heterodox views and external paths.
One does not instruct others to commit the ten unwholesome actions.
One does not instruct others to commit the five heinous crimes;
one does not praise the evils of others;
and one does not speak of worldly matters that lack purpose, such as frivolous laughter and play.
One does not teach others to have perverse faith in heterodox spirits or deities;
one does not engage in criticism regarding the merits or faults of people;
and one does not harbor anger or revile one's parents, teachers, elders, or virtuous friends.
Do not encourage others to commit evil deeds;
do not obstruct others from performing meritorious acts.
May your mouth always praise the Triple Gem.
He praised those who propagate the Dharma, describing their merits;
he showed people the retributions of good and evil deeds;
and he constantly taught that when the human body dies, the spiritual intelligence is not extinguished.
He constantly utters wholesome words to benefit others;
he constantly recites the twelve divisions of the Tathāgata’s honored sutras;
and he constantly declares that all sentient beings possess Buddha-nature and shall attain permanence, bliss, self, and purity.
They constantly teach others to serve their parents with filial piety and to revere teachers and elders.
They constantly exhort others to take refuge in the Triple Gem and to uphold the five precepts, the ten wholesome actions, and the six recollections.
They constantly praise and recite the sutras and chant all manner of wholesome teachings.
Constantly instructing others to draw near to virtuous friends and distance themselves from evil friends;
vowing that their mouths shall always speak of the immeasurable merits of the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) and the Buddha-stage (*buddhabhūmi*),
causing people to cultivate practices for the Pure Land to adorn the ultimate fruition.
He constantly teaches others to diligently pay homage to the Triple Gem;
he constantly teaches others to establish images and cultivate various offerings;
and he constantly teaches others to perform all manner of wholesome deeds as if their heads were on fire.
They constantly taught others to rescue the destitute and relieve the suffering without ceasing for even a moment.
Having finished making these oral vows,
they together prostrated themselves with their five limbs touching the ground with a sincere heart.
I take refuge in the Great Compassionate Father of the World.

Homage to Maitreya Buddha. Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha. Homage to Lokapuṣpa Buddha. Homage to Uccagāmin Buddha. Homage to Asaṅgavaiśāradya Buddha. Homage to Viśeṣajñānadarśana Buddha. Homage to Siṃhadaṃṣṭra Buddha. Homage to Liḍhabhū Buddha. Homage to Puṇyabhadra Buddha. Homage to Dharmapradīpasādhu Buddha. Homage to Maudgalyāyana Buddha. Homage to Aśokarāja Buddha. Homage to Manojña Buddha. Homage to Bodhipriya Buddha. Homage to Siṃhavikrīḍita Bodhisattva. Homage to Siṃhavijṛmbhita Bodhisattva. Homage to Anantakāya Bodhisattva. Homage to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. Furthermore, I take refuge in all the Three Jewels throughout the ten directions, as far as the limits of space.
I pray that by the power of your compassion, you will protect and sustain us, so that [Name] and others may fulfill their aspirations and attain the vows for enlightenment.

Furthermore, I pray that all sentient beings of the four modes of birth and six realms throughout the ten directions and the entirety of space may likewise do so. (The Dharma-gate of All Practices, The Dharma-gate of All Practices) Again, I pray for all sentient beings of the four modes of birth and six realms throughout the ten directions and the entirety of space.
From this point forward, after making these vows,
may each of you be able to fully perfect the dharma-gates of all practices,
and with sincere faith, cherish and revere the Three Jewels and the dharma-gates.
The Dharma-gate of firm resolve without harboring doubt;
the Dharma-gate of diligent repentance to sever and eliminate arising evil;
and the Dharma-gate of mindful regret for the sake of aspiring to purity.
The Dharma-gate for protecting the body through the purification of one's own mind;
the Dharma-gate for protecting the mouth by eternally purifying the four matters;
and the Dharma-gate for protecting the mind by not violating the three karmas.
The Dharma-gate of fulfilling all aspirations for bodhi;
the foremost Dharma-gate of compassion that does no harm;
and the Dharma-gate of transforming others to establish them in virtue and a mind of loving-kindness.
The Dharma-gate of not disparaging others' joy;
the Dharma-gate of not deceiving others with sincerity;
the Dharma-gate of wishing to extinguish the three evil realms through the Three Jewels.
The Dharma-gate of ultimate non-falsity and reality;
the Dharma-gate of abandoning the harm of pride regarding self and others;
the Dharma-gate of discarding fetters without hesitation.
The Dharma-gate of severing the intent for strife and litigation and being without contention;
the Dharma-gate of practicing equality in accordance with the True Dharma.
Furthermore, may all sentient beings be fully endowed with such immeasurable Dharma-gates.
The Dharma-gate of the Mind’s Inclination contemplates the mind as being like an illusion;
the Dharma-gate of the Mental Faculties abandons the roots of unwholesomeness;
the Dharma-gate of the Bases of Psychic Power renders body and mind light and agile.
The gateway of the faculty of faith does not seek to regress from the faculties;
the gateway of the faculty of vigor does not abandon the yoke of the wholesome;
the gateway of the faculty of mindfulness skillfully accomplishes the work of the Path.
The dharma-gate of the faculty of concentration is the right path for gathering the mind;
the dharma-gate of the faculty of wisdom is the contemplation of impermanence and emptiness;
the dharma-gate of the power of faith transcends the majestic might of Māra.
The dharma-gate of the power of progress is to go forth once and never return;
the dharma-gate of the power of mindfulness is never to forget or abandon;
the dharma-gate of the power of concentration is to extinguish all delusive thoughts.
The Dharma-gate of the Power of Wisdom circulates through coming and going;
the Dharma-gate of the Progression toward Awakening accumulates practices for the Buddha-way;
the Dharma-gate of Right Concentration attains samādhi.
In this Dharma-gate of the pure nature, one does not delight in other vehicles.
May all sentient beings fully possess these eighty thousand Dharma-gates of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas,
purifying Buddha-lands and exhorting and transforming those who are stingy and envious.
They fully deliver all from the eight difficult conditions of various evils;
they gather in those who are contentious and full of hatred;
and through the diligent practice of various virtues, they gather in those who are indolent.
With the supernormal power of concentrated mind, they gathered all distracted thoughts;
having finished making their vows,
they together prostrated themselves with their five limbs touching the ground with utmost sincerity.

I take refuge in the Great Compassionate Father of the World. Namo Maitreya Buddha. Namo Śākyamuni Buddha. Namo Dharmadeva-gaurava Buddha. Namo Cchinnabala Buddha. Namo Atibala Buddha. Namo Prajñāpuṣpa Buddha. Namo Dṛḍhasvara Buddha. Namo Sukhāvatī Buddha. Namo Svarthabuddhi Buddha. Namo Priyaviśuddha Buddha. Namo Hrī-lajjā-mukha Buddha. Namo Citracūḍa Buddha. Namo Kāmarati Buddha. Namo Vairocana Buddha. Namo Bhaiṣajyarāja Bodhisattva. Namo Bhaiṣajyasamudgata Bodhisattva. Namo Anantagātra Bodhisattva. Namo Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. Furthermore, I take refuge in all the Three Jewels throughout the ten directions, as far as the limits of space.
I pray that by the power of your compassion, you will rescue, protect,
and sustain all sentient beings of the three realms, six paths, and four modes of birth,
so that through the causes and conditions of the merit from now generating the bodhicitta and making vows within this Compassionate Dharma-Assembly Repentance, they may attain liberation.
Each and every one is fully endowed with merit and wisdom.

Having attained mastery over the mind through the power of spiritual penetrations (*abhijñā*) according to their wishes, and having already made their vows, they should now entrust [this teaching] for its circulation.
5. Entrustment, the fifth chapter. Today, the assembly of fellow practitioners at this site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*).
Having together made these vows for the sake of sentient beings within the six realms and four modes of birth,
we next entrust those beings to the great Bodhisattvas,
praying that they will compassionately accept and sustain them all.
By the causal conditions of the merit from this present repentance and making of vows,
may all sentient beings joyfully seek the unsurpassed field of blessings,
and with deep faith believe that offerings made to the Buddha yield immeasurable rewards.
May all sentient beings turn their minds with single-minded devotion toward the Buddha and fully attain immeasurable, pure karmic rewards.
May all sentient beings be free from avarice in the presence of all Buddhas.
Fully endowed with great generosity, they have nothing they do not cherish.
Furthermore, they vow that all sentient beings shall cultivate the unsurpassed field of merit in the presence of all Buddhas,
and leaving behind the aspirations of the two vehicles, they shall practice the bodhisattva path.
May they attain the unimpeded liberation and the knowledge of all modes of all Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, may all sentient beings plant inexhaustible roots of goodness before the Buddhas and attain the immeasurable merit and wisdom of the Buddhas.
Furthermore, may all sentient beings embrace profound wisdom and be fully endowed with the sovereign king of pure, unsurpassed knowledge.
Moreover, may all sentient beings attain unimpeded mastery wherever they roam.
May they attain the unimpeded supernormal powers that reach all places of the Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, may all sentient beings embrace the Mahāyāna and attain immeasurable kinds of wisdom, abiding therein immovably.
Furthermore, may all sentient beings fully accomplish the foremost field of merit and be able to give birth to the ground of all-knowledge.
Furthermore, may all sentient beings harbor no feelings of resentment toward any Buddha.
Planting all roots of goodness, they joyfully seek the wisdom of the Buddha;
furthermore, they vow that all sentient beings shall, by means of wondrous skillful expedients,
travel to all adorned buddha-fields.
In a single thought-moment,
they enter deeply into the Dharma-realm without weariness.
Furthermore, they vow that all sentient beings may attain a body beyond compare.
May they be able to travel everywhere throughout the worlds of the ten directions without weariness or fatigue.
Furthermore, may all sentient beings attain vast bodies and achieve unhindered movement at will;
may they obtain the adornments of the spiritual powers of all Buddhas and reach the ultimate further shore.
Within a single thought-moment, he manifested the sovereign spiritual powers of the Tathāgata pervading the entire realm of empty space.
Having thus completed this great vow,
it was as vast as the *dharmatā*.
Ultimately like empty space.
May all sentient beings attain the fulfillment of their aspirations and the vows for Bodhi.
Together, with a sincere heart, they prostrate themselves fully upon the ground.
If we, such-and-such individuals, are unable to save sentient beings while undergoing the retribution of suffering,
we entrust these sentient beings to the infinite and boundless Bodhisattvas of the Dharma-body who are unborn and pervade the entirety of the realm of empty space.
The Bodhisattvas of the untainted form-body, infinite and boundless, pervading the entirety of space;
the Bodhisattvas who have resolved their minds toward enlightenment, infinite and boundless, pervading the entirety of space;
and the Great Master Aśvaghoṣa, who upholds the True Dharma.
The Great Master Nāgārjuna, Bodhisattva of the Flourishing Semblance Dharma;
the Bodhisattva Boundless Body, who pervades the entirety of the realm of empty space in the ten directions;
and the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, the Savior from Suffering, who pervades the entirety of the realm of empty space in the ten directions.
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva,
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva,
and Siṃhavikrīḍita Bodhisattva.
Bodhisattva Siṃhavikrīḍita,
Bodhisattva Siṃhadhvaja,
and Bodhisattva Siṃhakāra.
The Bodhisattva Firm and Courageous Diligence,
the Bodhisattva Vajra Wisdom,
and the Bodhisattva Abandoning the Coverings of the Aggregates.
The Bodhisattva Śāntendriya,
the Bodhisattva Prajñottara,
and the Bodhisattva Sadāparivṛta.
Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja,
Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyasamudgata,
and Bodhisattva Gaganagañja.
Vajragarbha Bodhisattva,
Sadāparihita Bodhisattva,
and Anikṣiptadhura Bodhisattva.
Bodhisattva Wonderful Sound,
Bodhisattva Wondrous Virtue,
and Bodhisattva Jewel Moon.
The Bodhisattva Candraprabha,
the Bodhisattva Sadāprarudita,
and the Bodhisattva Trailokyavikrama further entrusted [this teaching] to all the bodhisattvas throughout the ten directions, as far as the limits of empty space.
May all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
by the power of their original vows and the power of their resolve to deliver sentient beings,
gather in and sustain all infinite and inexhaustible sentient beings throughout the ten directions.

May Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas not abandon any sentient being, sharing with them the mark of non-discrimination as true spiritual friends; may all sentient beings recognize the Bodhisattva’s kindness and draw near to make offerings to them.
May all bodhisattvas compassionately accept us,
causing all sentient beings to attain an upright mind and to follow after the bodhisattvas without ever being separated from them.
May all sentient beings follow the teachings of the Bodhisattvas without contravention;
may they attain a firm mind that does not abandon spiritual friends;
and may their minds be free from all defilements and indestructible.
May all sentient beings, for the sake of spiritual friends, not begrudge their own bodies or lives;
may they relinquish everything and never disobey their instructions.
May all sentient beings cultivate great loving-kindness and remain far removed from all evils.
Upon hearing the Buddha’s True Dharma, they are able to receive and uphold it entirely,
causing all sentient beings to share in the roots of goodness and karmic retributions of the bodhisattvas,
so that the practices and vows of the bodhisattvas reach ultimate purity.
Possessing supernatural powers and acting with sovereign mastery according to their will,
they ride upon the Mahāyāna until reaching the ultimate all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*),
remaining without weariness or rest throughout that interval.
Riding the vehicle of wisdom, one reaches the place of peace and security;
attaining the unimpeded vehicle, one achieves ultimate sovereignty.
From the beginning until now, having taken refuge in the Triple Gem, one severs doubt, gives rise to faith, repents, and resolves the mind [for enlightenment].
Manifesting the karmic retribution that emerges from hell,
one resolves resentment and rejoices within oneself,
making vows and dedicating merit.
Up until the entrustment,
may all the merit therein be bestowed as a gift upon all sentient beings throughout the ten directions and the entirety of the realm of empty space.
May the World-Honored One Maitreya appear to bear witness for me.
May the Buddhas of the ten directions take pity on and protect me;
may all that I repent and all that I vow be fully accomplished.
May all sentient beings, together with their compassionate father, be born in this land.
Having been present at the first assembly to hear the Dharma and realize the Way,
they are fully endowed with all merit and wisdom,
being no different from the various bodhisattvas.
Entering the Vajra-mind, he attained perfect enlightenment.
He praised the Buddha’s incantatory aspiration; he praised the Buddha’s incantatory aspiration: Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha—endowed with the three virtues.
Delivering immeasurable people and uprooting the suffering of birth and death,
by virtue of the causes and conditions of this present repentance and worship of the Buddha,
may all sentient beings each fully possess [these qualities].
May they attain the fulfillment of their aspirations as desired and realize Bodhi.
May the vows made today by [Name] and others be entirely identical to all the vows of all Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas throughout the ten directions and the entirety of space.
It is inexhaustible.
My present vow is likewise so:
as vast as the nature of phenomena (dharmatā).
Ultimately like space,
reaching the end of the future and exhausting all kalpas,
sentient beings can never be exhausted.
My vows are inexhaustible;
the worlds are inexhaustible;
my vows are inexhaustible.
Space is inexhaustible;
my vows are inexhaustible;
the nature of phenomena is inexhaustible.
My vows are inexhaustible;
nirvana is inexhaustible.
My vows are inexhaustible.
The appearance of Buddhas in the world is inexhaustible;
my vows are inexhaustible;
the wisdom of all Buddhas is inexhaustible.
My vows are inexhaustible;
the objects of my mind’s focus are inexhaustible;
my vows are inexhaustible.
The arising of wisdom is inexhaustible;
my vows are inexhaustible;
the varieties of worldly paths, the varieties of Dharma paths, and the varieties of the path of wisdom are inexhaustible.
My vows are inexhaustible;
only if these ten things were exhaustible could my vows be exhausted.
Homage to all the Noble Ones of the Three Vehicles.
The Ritual of Repentance at the Altar of Compassion, Scroll Ten.
